# airlock

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-24 — `airlock serve` tunnels, denies, or
> intercepts: the client's TLS ends at a leaf from airlock's tmpfs CA, verified
> TLS reopens to the real host, and an intercepted HTTP request has its
> credential swapped before it streams upstream.

## Scope

airlock is meant to become the single egress gateway of a sandboxed harness: LLM
providers, MCP servers, gh/glab APIs, guarded web and a git+ssh relay all leave
through it. LLM providers are one family of upstreams, not the center, so the
core stays protocol-agnostic: listener, client identity, policy, upstream with
credential injection, audit. It replaces CLIProxyAPI (`packages/cliproxyapi`) as
the credential proxy; both coexist until the harnesses are rewired
(`lib/ai/proxy` still resolves CLIProxyAPI instances only).

## Transport

A loopback TCP HTTP CONNECT forward proxy, reached through `HTTPS_PROXY`. Every
connection goes through airlock, but only the hosts an upstream lists in
`intercept` are decrypted; any other host is tunnelled or refused per
`unknownHosts`. A client identifies itself with the token in
`Proxy-Authorization: Basic`, so its proxy URL is
`http://<client>:<token>@127.0.0.1:<port>`.

Interception follows this order:

- airlock reads the ClientHello and requires its SNI to equal the CONNECT host,
  else it closes (`sni_mismatch`, `sni_missing`, `not_tls`). Otherwise a client
  could CONNECT to one host and speak TLS to another under that host's leaf.
- It opens TLS to the real host offering exactly the client's ALPN list,
  verified against the system store (`SSL_CERT_FILE` is honoured). Only then
  does it finish the client's handshake, offering only the protocol the upstream
  chose, so ALPN matches end to end.
- Startup loads client tokens and every distinct credential named by a grant
  once, collecting every unreadable or empty file before serving. Credentials
  with no grant stay on disk. A grant currently selects its first credential;
  fallback to a later credential is future work.
- Interception parses HTTP on the negotiated protocol, opens one verified
  upstream connection of the same kind, and streams request and response bodies
  as frames. It preserves method, path, query, status, version, headers, and
  body bytes; HTTP/2 requests are given the absolute `https` URI that protocol
  requires.
- Before injection, every request drops client `Authorization` and `x-api-key`
  values plus hop-by-hop fields named by `Connection`. An OAuth credential is
  injected as a sensitive Authorization bearer header; an API key is injected as
  a sensitive x-api-key header. Other request headers stay unchanged.
- A valid HTTP/1 upgrade keeps `Upgrade` and `Connection: Upgrade`, forwards the
  101, and then bridges the two upgraded byte streams. Other upgrades and
  hop-by-hop fields are removed. An upstream send or handshake failure on an
  applicable request becomes 502.
- The CONNECT audit carries `sni`, `alpn`, the selected credential, and request
  count, never body bytes or secrets. Its byte counters cover completed TLS
  application writes, including HTTP framing, rather than body payload alone.
  Normal connections retain bounded `close_notify` shutdown; an upgraded stream
  is relayed until one peer closes.

The CA lives in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/airlock-<port>/` (0700): `ca.key`
(PKCS#8, 0600) and `ca.pem` (0644), ECDSA P-256 with `pathlen:0` and no name
constraints. Startup refuses an unset or relative `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, one not
owned 0700 by the user, or on Linux one that is not tmpfs or ramfs; the CA
directory itself must pass the same checks. The tmpfs is what rotates the CA at
every reboot; it survives airlock restarts within a boot. Startup also refuses a
symlink in place of either directory or file, a lone `ca.key` or `ca.pem`, a
group- or other-readable key, or a key that does not match the certificate, and
never writes over an existing file. `ca.pem` is the one file meant to leave
airlock: the sandbox will trust it, never the host's trust store. Leaves are
minted per intercepted host on demand, each with its own key, for 7 days, and
are held only in memory.

Why CONNECT and not a base URL, measured 2026-10-24 against Claude Code 2.1.309
with a local CONNECT proxy intercepting TLS and a fake token, offline:

- Through `HTTPS_PROXY` with no base URL, the `/v1/messages` body carries the
  first-party billing tag with its signature (`cch=…`), and the request sends
  `Authorization: Bearer <CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN>`.
- With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set, the same tag has no `cch=`, and Claude Code
  turns off first-party features. That is why CLIProxyAPI has to re-forge it.
- Every CONNECT carried `Proxy-Authorization` from the userinfo in
  `HTTPS_PROXY`, so one port can tell clients apart.
- All traffic went to `api.anthropic.com`, on many `/api/*` paths besides
  `/v1/messages`. An intercepted host must pass every path through and swap the
  token wherever it appears; an allowlist of paths would break features.

The harness therefore holds only fake client credentials, such as a disposable
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; airlock reads the real provider credential from its
runtime files when it binds and substitutes it on every intercepted request.

## Not a security boundary yet

airlock runs as the harness's uid. `ai.jail` binds `/` into the jail, so the
harness can read airlock's runtime directory, its CA key, its state and the
secret files the launcher writes there. Until airlock runs under a separate uid
or outside the harness's VM, it keeps real credentials out of the harness's
environment and config, not out of its reach.

## Nix wiring

`modules/instances.nix` is one module for both backends, through
`packages/ai-module/lib/instances.nix`. Each instance is the `ai.services` entry
`airlock-<name>` running `airlock serve --config "$AIRLOCK_CONFIG"`; its port
and service name are claimed by the helper.

`settings` mirrors airlock-core's `RawConfig` field for field. The render
renames three keys (`stateDir` → `state_dir`, `unknownHosts` → `unknown_hosts`,
a client's `token` → `token_file`) and nothing else. Field validity (id
spelling, references between clients, credentials and upstreams, empty grants)
is airlock-core's job, not the Nix types'. Add a field on both sides at once:
`airlock-config-roundtrip` runs `check-config` on a rendered sample, and
`deny_unknown_fields` refuses a key Rust does not know.

Every client token and credential file is `redact.types.secretFile`. The
launcher writes each value to a 0600 file in its runtime directory and fills the
config's placeholder with that path; airlock-core requires the path to be
absolute and reads it at start.

## Settled — do not relitigate

- **A unix socket with Claude Code's `ANTHROPIC_UNIX_SOCKET` placeholder mode is
  not the main path.** The socket path under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unknown at
  evaluation, and the mode serves only Claude Code; CONNECT serves every client
  that honours `HTTPS_PROXY`.
- **Base-URL mode is not the main path.** Claude Code drops `cch` behind
  `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, so a subscription request would have to be forged.
- **No Postgres for now.** Home Manager has no user-level Postgres module, so it
  would break Home Manager and devenv parity. Storage, when it lands, is SQLite
  in `stateDir` behind a trait.
